extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for journal editors on using Publons and related practices to find, screen, recruit, motivate, and recognize peer reviewers while tracking editorial contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors can use Publons to find reviewers for participating journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Publons to source reviewers; the platform aggregates reviewers' peer review records across journals so editors can discover potential reviewers. Combine with other approaches rather than relying solely on ad hoc methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen reviewers for qualifications and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should screen reviewers for qualifications and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publons and the Partner Dashboard can assist screening, but editors remain responsible for verifying expertise and conflicts. Screening helps ensure quality reviews and protect integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact reviewers directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors need reliable ways to contact potential reviewers directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publons supports contacting reviewers; reducing ad hoc communication improves speed. Ensure contact methods respect reviewers' preferences and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivate reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should actively motivate reviewers to accept and complete reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because incentives for publishing outweigh incentives for reviewing, recognition (e.g., via Publons) can motivate reviewers. Consider explicit recognition, feedback, and converting reviewers into readers/authors/repeat reviewers as incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reviewers and editors (make reviewing measurable and rewarding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn peer review and editorial contributions into measurable, rewarding activities so reviewers and editors receive recognition for their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Publons to keep a record of peer review and editorial work, ensuring recognition even if reviews are anonymous or articles are not published. Showcase this proof of service to support career progression and institutional/funder consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer anonymity by default
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, only the journal name and year of the review show on Publons to maintain the anonymity of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect reviewers' choice to opt in; do not expose identifying details unless the reviewer consents. This balances recognition with confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reviewer opt-in for profile recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must opt in for their review to be added to their Publons profile; they are not automatically signed up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-in preserves reviewer autonomy and confidentiality. Editors should inform reviewers about the option and how it works when inviting or acknowledging reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add reviews from non-partnered journals with proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can add reviews for non-partnered journals by sending proof (e.g., 'Thank you for reviewing' email) to Publons for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send proof to [email protected]; Publons checks the proof and updates the profile. This enables comprehensive reviewer records beyond partnered journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Partner Dashboard to manage and grow reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should use the Partner Dashboard features to understand and grow their reviewing pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner Dashboard provides features to find, screen, contact, and recruit reviewers. Register for free monthly webinars to learn available features and best practices for growing and managing reviewer pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide confidential editor feedback and recognize excellent reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should provide feedback to reviewers to help them improve and give recognition for reviews that show extra effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Publons' editor feedback and 'excellent review' feature to give confidential feedback and explicit recognition. Constructive confidential feedback helps raise review quality and rewards high-effort reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track editorial work and showcase service
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should create a free Publons profile to track their peer review and editorial work and showcase this proof of service and standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking editorial contributions helps demonstrate service for promotion, funding, and institutional recognition. Encourage editors to maintain up-to-date records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider early career researchers as reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers can be reliable, high-quality, responsive, and timely reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't dismiss early career researchers; they may be eager to build their profile. Source these reviewers via Publons Academy graduates and provide mentoring/feedback as needed to ensure review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reviewing to protect quality control and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: If contributors do not get credit for reviewing, it weakens quality control, slows the process of finding reviewers, and can result in more poor-quality reviews letting misleading research through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving proper credit and recognition for reviewing mitigates these risks by improving reviewer supply and incentivizing careful, quality reviews. Use recognition systems (like Publons) to address incentive imbalances between publishing and reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote peer review recognition for institutional/funder consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Make peer review and editorial work measurable so institutions and funders can take them into account for career progression and funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By providing verifiable records of reviewing efforts, editors and publishers can help institutionalize peer review as a valued scholarly output, increasing incentives for high-quality reviewing.
